title.narrative: Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises to adopt new business models, technology and techniques to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative: 1. The Sustaining Competitive and Responsible Enterprises (SCORE) programme has been operationalised to promote productivity, fostering training on innovation and workplace cooperation for SMEs to create more and decent jobs. a. The SCORE programme has trained 34 enterprises on workplace cooperation and cleaner production. In 2021 75% of the enterprises have reported increased productivity; 100% enterprises reported tracking of key performance indicators; decrease in defects; improved cooperation and communication between workers and management and reduced work absenteeism. b. In May 2021 the Zimbabwe Productivity and Continuous Improvement Centre has been established by national SCORE Trainers to further provide training services to local enterprises. 2. In 2020-2021 a GreenEnterPRIZE Innovation Challenge was run to promote entrepreneurship and SME development in the green economy: a. By April 2020, 78 SMEs are providing sustainable green products and services in agriculture and forestry, renewable energy, waste management, food processing, arts and crafts and small-scale manufacturing. In 2021 a network of 12 providers has been supported to deliver green business development services to SMEs. Three How-To-Do Manuals on business formalisation, workplace OSH and managing and growing green businesses were adopted in May 2021. 3. Zimbabwe has operationalised the Anchor Enterprise Business Model to promote entrepreneurship and SME development in the horticulture and edible insect(mopane worm) value chains in rural areas: a. Over the period 2020-2021 two anchor enterprises-Mutoko Royal Fruits and Vegies (Pvt) Ltd in Mutoko to primarily value-add horticultural produce; and Mvelelo (Pvt) Ltd in Beitbridge for processing mopane worms have been registered. The enterprises are co-owned and integrate primary producers from local communities into the horticulture and edible insects value chains with support national and local government. 1. In 2020-2021 the ILO provided technical assistance through the SWEDEN funded GreenENTERPRIZE programme towards the training of 2218 staff (63% workers, 25% female) from the 34 enterprises. A trainer of trainers (ToT) course was run for 10, out of which 9 successfully completed the training and 7 have been certified. 2. In 2020-2021 the ILO ran a 3-series national Innovation Challenge that covered over 700 subscribers with 78 entrepreneurs winning both financial and non-financial prizes. 632 non-winners received green business training. In 2020 the ILO customised the Generate Your Business (GYB) methodology to be delivered via radio and WhatsApp messaging resulting in about 1300 people including 42% in rural areas benefiting from orientation towards innovation and generating green business ideas. 3. In 2020 with support from the AfDB and the Government of Zimbabwe the ILO designed the Anchor Enterprise Model in partnership with local communities and key stakeholders; delivered business management and financial literacy training derived from the ILO SIYB methodology and technical training for primary producers to enhance production. The two received capital equipment including factory shells and equipment valued at $1.4 million and mentoring and seed capital to start-up operations.The enterprises are now supplying value-added products to local retail markets increasing incomes and creating jobs in the local communities.
